rows.question: Briefly explain AI engineering.
rows.raw: {"answer": "The technical field of designing, building, evaluating, and operating useful applications and systems using pretrained foundation models (mainly LLMs) as components. It focuses on selecting models, connecting them to data and tools, and iterating on evaluation and improvement, rather than building models from scratch.", "needs_review": false}

rows.question: What is Token?
rows.raw: {"answer": "The smallest unit an LLM uses to process text. Text is split into fragments of words or characters. API charges, rate limits, and context window sizes are often counted in tokens. Tokenization varies by language; for example, Japanese tends to require more tokens per character than English.", "needs_review": false}

rows.question: Briefly explain Prompt.
rows.raw: {"answer": "Input text passed to an LLM. In addition to questions, it can include roles, constraints, output formats, and examples to guide the output.", "needs_review": false}

rows.question: What is Hallucination?
rows.raw: {"answer": "The phenomenon of an LLM generating plausible content that is factually incorrect or nonexistent. It is more likely when asked about things the model does not know, such as recent information or organization- or course-specific details. Mitigations include consulting external data through tools, asking for evidence, and detecting errors through evaluation.", "needs_review": false}

rows.question: Briefly explain API key.
rows.raw: {"answer": "A secret string that identifies the person calling an API. If it leaks, someone else can consume your usage allowance, so do not put it directly in code, commit it, or paste it into chat. In this course, register it as a Codespaces secret and read it through the GEMINI_API_KEY environment variable.", "needs_review": false}

rows.question: What is GitHub Codespaces?
rows.raw: {"answer": "A cloud development environment provided by GitHub. Open VS Code in a browser and immediately use an environment configured by the repository. Personal accounts have a monthly free allowance; if you do not stop the Codespace when idle, it continues consuming that allowance.", "needs_review": false}

rows.question: Briefly explain Codespaces secret.
rows.raw: {"answer": "A secret value registered in your GitHub account settings. It is passed as an environment variable when you start Codespaces for a selected repository. When registering it, select the repository you will use (your own fork). If registered while a Codespace is running, restart the Codespace.", "needs_review": false}

rows.question: What is Pull Request (PR)?
rows.raw: {"answer": "A mechanism for requesting that changes from one branch be merged into another. It supports reviewing differences, comments, and displaying automated test results. Submit work for this course as a PR from your working branch to main within your own fork.", "needs_review": false}

rows.question: Briefly explain Code completion.
rows.raw: {"answer": "A feature in which AI suggests code to follow partially written code or comments. Accept suggestions with Tab or a similar action. Suggestions may be incorrect, so read and understand them before accepting.", "needs_review": false}

rows.question: What is Fine-tuning?
rows.raw: {"answer": "Further training a pretrained model on data suited to a specific task or format. It is suitable for teaching output format, tone, or behavior in a specific domain. For up-to-date facts, consulting external data through tools or RAG is often more suitable.", "needs_review": false}

rows.question: Briefly explain PEFT.
rows.raw: {"answer": "An umbrella term for methods that train only a small subset of model parameters or a small set of added parameters instead of all parameters. This can greatly reduce GPU memory and storage requirements. LoRA is a representative example.", "needs_review": false}

rows.question: What is QLoRA?
rows.raw: {"answer": "A method that saves memory by quantizing base-model weights to, for example, 4 bits, then trains with LoRA. This lets smaller GPUs handle larger models. In the Lecture 02 exercises, the model fits in GPU memory, so we train with LoRA and compare memory and output differences when loading in 4-bit in the advanced section.", "needs_review": false}

rows.question: Briefly explain Learning rate.
rows.raw: {"answer": "A hyperparameter that determines how far parameters move in one update. Too large a value makes training unstable; too small a value slows progress.", "needs_review": false}

rows.question: What is Hugging Face Hub?
rows.raw: {"answer": "A platform for sharing and downloading public models and datasets. Used to obtain open-weight models and publish LoRA adapters.", "needs_review": false}

rows.question: Briefly explain Agent loop.
rows.raw: {"answer": "The process of passing input to the model → executing any tool calls returned by the model → returning results to the model, repeated until the model gives a final answer. Multiple LLM calls for one question have a substantial effect on time, charges, and rate limits.", "needs_review": false}

rows.question: What is Structured output?
rows.raw: {"answer": "A mechanism for receiving model outputs according to specified types or a JSON schema. This makes programmatic postprocessing easier. In Pydantic AI, specify a Pydantic model in output_type.", "needs_review": false}

rows.question: Briefly explain Pi.
rows.raw: {"answer": "An open-source (MIT-licensed) coding agent that runs in the terminal. It has minimal features and a minimal system prompt, designed for users to extend. Version 1.0 was released in October 2026. Its npm package name is @earendil-works/pi-coding-agent.", "needs_review": false}

rows.question: What is MCP (Model Context Protocol)?
rows.raw: {"answer": "An open standard protocol connecting AI applications to external tools and data sources. Tools exposed through an MCP server can be used in a common way from compatible agents and editors (MCP clients). In Lecture 05, you will experience this by turning glossary search into an MCP server.", "needs_review": false}

rows.question: Briefly explain Human-in-the-loop.
rows.raw: {"answer": "Incorporating human confirmation or approval into agent processing. Used before operations that are difficult to undo, such as writing or sending data. In Pydantic AI, tools with requires_approval=True support this.", "needs_review": false}

rows.question: What is answer.md?
rows.raw: {"answer": "The file for recording exercise and homework results for each AIE2026 lecture. Located at lectures/NN/answer.md. Record the level attempted, what you did, results, and observations, then submit by opening a PR from your working branch to main in your own fork.", "needs_review": false}

rows.question: Briefly explain Default model.
rows.raw: {"answer": "The standard model for AIE2026 exercises and homework, chosen with free-tier rate limits and stable course operation in mind. You may switch models with the AIE_MODEL environment variable or use your own API subscription.", "needs_review": false}

rows.question: What is MCP client?
rows.raw: {"answer": "The component that connects to MCP servers, passes their tools to the model, and calls tools as directed by the model. Agent programs (Pydantic AI's MCPToolset) and editors or applications such as Copilot Chat, Claude Desktop, and Cursor can serve as clients. A benefit of MCP is using the same server from different clients.", "needs_review": false}

rows.question: Briefly explain mcpServers configuration.
rows.raw: {"answer": "A configuration file listing MCP servers to use. For each server, specify a name and a startup command (stdio) or destination URL (HTTP). Claude Desktop, Cursor, and Pydantic AI read the same mcpServers format (VS Code / Copilot Chat uses servers). This course uses app/mcp_servers.json. Adding tools with just a few configuration lines is central to the MCP experience.", "needs_review": false}
